chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

the man against whom a right is claimed and there is no evidence for the claimant, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is sworn an oath, or the oath is returned to the owner of the right; if he does not do so, then he has no right.'

key_terms.يُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ: against whom a right is claimed

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a claimant has no evidence to support their claim in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the mechanism of *al-yamin* (oath) in Shia jurisprudence, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to evidentiary standards in civil cases. It establishes that the burden of proof can be shifted via oath-taking, a principle rooted in the Prophetic tradition 'The claimant must prove, or the oath is on the defendant,' emphasizing procedural justice when witnesses are absent. This method underscores the flexibility of Shia legal theory in resolving disputes through solemn affirmation rather than rigid evidentiary requirements.
